advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm docker_apparent_bytes is intentionally exposed only in the log line and not as its own CloudWatch metric for trend comparison.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:955 `docker_storage_bytes` publishes docker_total_bytes (allocated)
infra/scripts/observability.sh:1003 apparent only appears in the rebar-health log line, not a put-metric-data call
The change introduces docker_apparent_bytes as a first-class census output (DOCKER_DU_APPARENT) but exposes it only via logger
advisory.finding: The docker_du_seconds/docker_du_ok metrics are published (lines 950-953) and gate docker_storage_bytes and residue, but the docker_apparent_bytes value itself is never published as its own CloudWatch metric — only consumed to derive docker_unaccounted_bytes. If a future operator wants to compare allocated vs apparent trends over time (the whole point of this ticket's distinction), only the log line carries apparent bytes. This is a design observation, not a defect: confirm the log-line-only exposure of apparent bytes is intentional.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm no CloudWatch anomaly-detection band or dashboard baseline depends on the pre-change (allocated-based) docker_unaccounted_bytes series before deploying the apparent-based numerator.
evidence: infra/scripts/observability.sh:991 `docker_unaccounted=$(( docker_apparent_bytes - docker_accounted_bytes ))`
runbook: `The residue was 1,183,214,875 apparent bytes, not the 2,685,139,712-byte allocated-minus-ledger value.`
The alarm uses a static `treat_missing_data`/evaluation window (monitoring_autodeploy.tf) but no note about the historical-series break for CloudWatch anomaly detection or dashboards.
advisory.finding: docker_unaccounted_bytes changes its numerator from allocated bytes to apparent bytes, producing a step discontinuity in the published CloudWatch metric series; any anomaly-detection band, dashboard, or historical comparison keyed on the pre-change values will see a spurious drop (~1.5 GB on the cited 2026-09-05 box: 2.685 GB allocated-residue vs 1.183 GB apparent-residue) at deploy time.
scenarios: An operator or CloudWatch anomaly-detection model comparing recent docker_unaccounted_bytes to a baseline collected before this deploy.

advisory.finding: The new hardlink de-duplication (`key=$1":"$2; if (seen[key]++) next`, counting a file once per device+inode) is never exercised: every `find` stub row uses a distinct inode (1, 2, 3), so a regression that dropped the dedup — double-counting a hardlinked layer file — would not be caught by any test.
merged_from: The overlay2 subtotal is now SUMMED over the overlay2 subtree (`path == root "/overlay2" || index(path, root "/overlay2/") == 1`), replacing the old single-row read, but no test emits any nested path under `overlay2/`; every stub emits only a single row whose path is exactly `<root>/overlay2`, so the subtree-summation branch is never exercised.
scenarios: A future edit removes or breaks the `seen[key]` guard; hardlinked cross-layer files are double-counted, inflating docker_storage_bytes and docker_unaccounted_bytes; no test fails.
